Curated Destination

Kerala

Kerala, often referred to as "God's Own Country," is a tropical paradise known for its palm-fringed backwaters, misty hill stations, and rich cultural heritage.

Experience the tranquility of a houseboat stay in Alleppey, the aromatic tea plantations of Munnar, and the traditional Kathakali performances in Kochi.

Kerala offers a perfect blend of relaxation and adventure, making it an ideal destination for families, honeymooners, and solo travelers alike.

Places in Kerala

Discover the remarkable places that make this destination special.

Place

Cochin

Popularly known as the Queen of the Arabian Sea, Cochin does live up to its name. Set among lagoons, islands and waterways on Kerala’s Malabar Coast, this historic port has been welcoming travellers, traders and adventurers for centuries. Arabs, Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch and British all left their mark here, creating a fascinating blend of cultures that remains woven into the character of the city. The atmospheric lanes of Fort Cochin, where elegant colonial buildings, old churches, spice warehouses and shaded streets evoke another era and you could wander past the iconic Chinese fishing nets on the waterfront and visit the 16th-century St Francis Church. Mattencherry is totally different vibe, with the former royal quarter of Mattancherry, with its spice-scented bazaars and historic Jewish synagogue. For a more intimate perspective, take to the water. A private boat trip through Cochin’s backwaters reveals a quieter world of coconut palms, narrow canals and small villages, while an evening performance of Kathakali, Kerala’s extraordinary classical dance-drama, offers an unforgettable introduction to the state’s rich artistic traditions. Cochin is the perfect introduction to Kerala – not simply a gateway to the backwaters and spice country beyond, but a captivating destination in its own right. Spend a few days here and the layers begin to reveal themselves: a city of old-world elegance, fascinating cultural encounters and the gentle rhythms of life on India's tropical Malabar Coast.

Place

Kovalam

Kovalam is where Kerala meets the sea. Once a sleepy fishing village, its palm-fringed beaches now offer a wonderfully unhurried place to pause and savour the coast. Watch fishermen bring in their catch at dawn, wander along the shoreline as the light softens, or retreat to an Ayurvedic treatment inspired by Kerala’s centuries-old traditions. Away from the beaches, village life continues much as it has for generations. For those seeking something beyond the conventional beach holiday, Kovalam offers a gentle immersion in Kerala’s coastal rhythm — a place to breathe, slow down and simply watch the Arabian Sea roll towards the shore.

Wayanad

Set among the mist-shrouded hills of Kerala’s Western Ghats, Wayanad offers a more secluded and deeply immersive side of the state. Lush forests, coffee and spice plantations, waterfalls and remote valleys create a landscape made for slowing down and exploring at an unhurried pace. Beyond its natural beauty, Wayanad is home to several indigenous communities whose traditions remain closely connected to the forest. With the guidance of knowledgeable local hosts, a carefully arranged tribal visit offers an opportunity to learn about their distinctive customs, crafts, food and intimate understanding of the natural world. Add walks through plantations, wildlife excursions and the enigmatic Edakkal Caves, lets you enjoy Wayanad where nature, culture and rural life come together with a sense of discovery.

Periyar National Park

Set high in Kerala’s Cardamom Hills, Periyar National Park is one of South India’s most atmospheric wildlife destinations. At its heart lies the tranquil Periyar Lake, where forested slopes descend to the water and elephants frequently gather along the shore. With a mix of tropical evergreen, grassland and Shola forest, the Periyar National park is home to a variety of animals, mammals and birds. The park is home to Asian elephants, gaur, sambar, wild boar and an extraordinary variety of birdlife, while elusive tigers and leopards inhabit the surrounding forests. Rather than simply ticking off wildlife sightings, Periyar is about experiencing the forest: take a boat journey across the lake, walk with trained naturalists, or venture deeper into the reserve on a guided nature experience. The result is an immersive encounter with Kerala’s wilderness, best enjoyed at a leisurely pace.

Kumarakom

On the shores of the Vembanad lake lies this cluster of islands, with crisscross canal, palm fringed paddy field and a very unique way of life. It's one of the main places to go to to explore the fames backwaters of Kerala. Once the area could only be accessed by boats but with the advent of bridges the navigation between the shores have changed but very little has changed in the way the people go about their lives. This is a great place to experience real life on the backwaters. Life in Kumarakom revolves around the water. Traditional fishing boats and canoes move through narrow waterways, while village communities continue age-old activities such as fishing, coir making, toddy tapping and rice cultivation. Exploring these waterways by canoe provides an intimate view of everyday life, far beyond the larger houseboat routes.The nearby Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary is a haven for birdwatchers, attracting both resident and migratory birds. The surrounding Vembanad wetlands also support a remarkable variety of wildlife and plant life.

Place

Munnar

Set among the misty mountains of Kerala, Munnar is a landscape of rolling tea estates, deep valleys and forested peaks. Explore the story of tea with visits to working plantations, meet local artisans at Sristi, a social enterprise supporting people with disabilities through traditional crafts, and venture into the hills on scenic walks and treks. From gentle trails through tea country to more challenging climbs towards Meesapulimala, Munnar offers an intimate way to experience Kerala’s highlands, its people and its extraordinary natural beauty.

Place

Thattekad Bird Sanctuary

Set beside the Periyar River, Thattekad is one of Kerala’s most rewarding destinations for nature lovers and birdwatchers. The surrounding lowland forests and plantations harbour an extraordinary variety of birdlife, including endemic species such as the Malabar grey hornbill, Malabar parakeet and SriLanka frogmouth. Early morning walks reveal a landscape alive with birdsong, butterflies and forest sounds, while gentle trails lead through a lush mosaic of woodland, streams and plantations. Thattekad is one of main spots for a truly rewarding off-beat experience where our team can offer you some unique walks, kayaking and local experiences.
